The assistant also suggested adjusting the oats-to-water ratio, adding flavorings, and saving or discarding the oat pulp.

For homemade teriyaki sauce, the assistant suggested combining 1/2 cup soy sauce, 1/4 cup sake (or dry sherry or mirin), 1/4 cup granulated sugar, 2 tablespoons rice vinegar, 2 tablespoons grated ginger, 2 minced garlic cloves, and optionally 1 tablespoon sesame oil. Whisk the soy sauce, sake, sugar, and vinegar until the sugar dissolves; add ginger and garlic; bring to a boil, then simmer on low for 5–7 minutes until slightly thickened; remove from heat, stir in optional sesame oil, cool, and strain. The assistant said it keeps refrigerated in an airtight container for up to two weeks.

For Chicken Yakitori, the assistant recommended bite-size chicken pieces about 1–1.5 inches (2.5–3.8 cm), seasoned with salt equal to 1–2% of chicken weight, sugar equal to 0.5–1% of chicken weight, and optionally 1–2 tablespoons sake or mirin. Refrigerate for at least 30 minutes and up to 2 hours; pat dry before grilling. The assistant suggested bamboo skewers soaked in water for at least 30 minutes or flat, wide steel skewers to stop chicken spinning, and grilling at about 400°F for 5–7 minutes per side, glazing with teriyaki sauce in the final minute.

For Salmon Teriyaki, the assistant recommended Atlantic, sockeye, or king salmon; pat fillets dry, remove skin if desired, and use portions about 1–1.5 inches (2.5–3.8 cm) thick. Grill over medium-high heat, around 400°F, for 4–6 minutes per side, and brush with teriyaki sauce during the final minute.

On 2023-06-20, the user asked what a CEP engine and an OMS are in algorithmic trading. The assistant explained that a Complex Event Processing (CEP) engine analyzes high-volume streaming data in real time to identify opportunities and generate signals, while an Order Management System (OMS) manages the trade lifecycle, including sending orders to brokers or exchanges, risk management, compliance, and reporting. The CEP engine’s signals can be sent to the OMS for execution.

On 2023-06-20, the user asked about the components of an algorithmic trading system. The assistant listed data sources, market-data storage, trading algorithms, risk-management tools, an execution platform, and backtesting and simulation tools. Data sources can include exchanges, market-data providers, and news feeds; algorithms analyze data to generate signals; execution platforms automate trades, often through broker APIs; and backtesting and simulation test strategies against historical data before live deployment.
